AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to allowing for students in

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1880

SPONSOR: SKOUFIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to allowing for students
in postsecondary education experience or transition program to receive
awards from the tuition assistance program

 
PURPOSE:

To correct an inequity in the current law by making students with intel-
lectual disabilities who are enrolled in a postsecondary education expe-
rience or transition programs eligible for assistance from the Tuition
Assistance Program (TAP).

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends Section 602 of the education law to add a new subdivi-
sion requiring the Commissioner of Education for students with intellec-
tual disabilities enrolled in an approved postsecondary education expe-
rience or transition program to receive financial assistance from the
Tuition Assistance Program (TAP).

Section 2: Amends Section 667 of the education law to add a new subdivi-
sion defining the meaning of "postsecondary education experience or
transition program" and states that TAP awards shall be made available
to qualified students with intellectual disabilities who are enrolled in
an approved postsecondary education experience or transition program.
Also defines "students with intellectual disabilities" for purposes of
this section.

Section 3: Sets effective date

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Postsecondary education experiences or transition programs are important
avenues for young adults with disabilities who seek to improve their
future through higher education and vocational preparation. The mission
of these programs enjoys large support among New Yorkers. Howev-
er,because these programs are generally non-degree programs, students
are not eligible for financial support through the Tuition Assistance
Program. Federally funded aid for non-degree programs serving intellec-
tually disabled students became available through the Higher Education
Opportunity Act (HEOA) of 2008, which authorized the US Department of
Education to certify certain program as Comprehensive Training and Post-
secondary Program or CTPs. Programs meeting CTP eligibility requirements
have their Title IV Financial Aid agreement with the federal government
amended to permit disbursing select forms of aid - Pell grants and Work
Study - to non-degree seeking students with ID/DD.

It is reasonable for New York State to support these programs and
students' efforts to better themselves by mirroring the example: set
forth by the federal government. This bill makes TAP funds available to
intellectually disabled students attending a qualified postsecondary
education experience or transition program.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

Senate

2020 - S5071, Referred to Finance

2021-2022- S1786A, Referred to Finance

Assembly

2020 - No Assembly Same-As

2021-2022- A3032, Referred to Higher Education

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
